title: One Time Toolbar Filter Density Audit

reasons: The operator called out wasted top space, oversized pills, subcategory/filter consistency, desktop/mobile behavior, and role-specific One Time views.
The affected surface crosses Operations, provider, parent, student, and member review routes, so current-state measurement must precede implementation.
A repeatable harness lets Agent Mode and Codex compare the same top-section measurements instead of relying on unstructured chat output.
affected_product_surfaces: Operations One Time workspace top rail
One Time provider review topbar and mailbox toolbar
One Time parent review topbar and filters
One Time student review topbar and board filters
likely_external_provider_blockers: No Stripe, email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, DNS, credential, payment, access, provider, or production-data mutation is approved in this audit.
Authenticated live Rabbi/provider mailbox data remains privacy-gated; this audit measures layout only.
ramble_router.next_exact_packet: Create a small implementation packet only for the highest-impact toolbar/filter defect confirmed by this audit.

operator_intent_summary: The One Time and shared portal top sections should be compact, logical, role-consistent, and usable on desktop and mobile, with side-panel categories, top subcategories, filters, and action buttons appearing in predictable positions without wasted space, clipping, overlap, or uncontrolled scrolling.
raw_quotes: the top toolbar, I don't even know if it's called a toolbar, the top section, is just, there's a lot of empty space
it's just not spaced out well. It's just wasted space, and in mobile, it's not gonna run well
the top section is like this top toolbar with like these pills that just takes up too space too much space
all of the the side panels the categories and the top all of those things in the filters across every single workspace is all going to be positioned the same way
when I say a million-dollar app ... everything needs to be consistent

decisions_captured.decision: Run a current-state toolbar/filter density audit before applying global CSS or IA changes.

out_of_scope: No external sends, live email, WhatsApp, Telegram, payment, Stripe, access grant, DNS, provider, credential, Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, or production-data mutation.
No broad rewrite of the Operations shell, parent portal, student portal, provider portal, or member portal in this audit packet.
No authenticated billing, attendance, transcript, Rabbi-reference, or password reset implementation.
No claim that visual work is complete merely because measurements were captured.
affected_surfaces: Operations One Time workspace top rail and local toolbars
One Time provider review topbar and mailbox toolbar
One Time parent review topbar and filter rows
One Time student review topbar and board filter rows

inspection_targets: public/css/one-time-shared-review.css already constrains One Time portal topbars and mobile review actions.
public/css/one-time-operations.css already includes scoped repairs for several One Time Operations rails and toolbars.
Existing shared-review smoke catches whole-page horizontal overflow but does not measure top cluster height, row count, clipped control text, touch target size, or overlap.
Agent Mode reports have been inconsistent unless the prompt names exact navigation paths and a drop-off/reporting contract.
known_blockers: Operations routes need an Operations session cookie; the audit skips those checks only if credentials are unavailable.
The audit may produce findings that span several routes and must be split into small implementation packets before CSS changes.

expanded_phrases.million-dollar app: Measured consistency: stable category/subcategory/filter hierarchy, no uncontrolled horizontal overflow, aligned controls, compact top chrome, mobile 44px touch targets, role-appropriate content, screenshot proof, and deploy/live-smoke gates for app-visible changes.
expanded_phrases.professional: Predictable spacing, consistent controls, route-specific information architecture, no debug/admin leakage in user views, and no subjective done status without evidence.
expanded_phrases.clean: Top sections are compact and organized, with no redundant row stacking, no clipped labels, and no wasted first-viewport space.
expanded_phrases.sloppy: Any overlap, clipped control, inconsistent height spread, confusing row order, uncontrolled scroll, or irrelevant setup/admin content is a visual defect requiring a finding.
expanded_phrases.toolbar: The audit treats brand topbars, top filter rails, tab lists, local toolbars, mailbox toolbar, board toolbar, and filter rows as measurable top-section controls.
expanded_phrases.filters: Filters must be in predictable top rows or controlled mobile overflow, not scattered or duplicated without role meaning.
expanded_phrases.buttons should be equal: Top controls must have consistent heights and at least 44px mobile tap targets.
expanded_phrases.wasted space: First meaningful content and toolbar cluster height are measured against desktop and mobile thresholds.
expanded_phrases.mobile: 390px and 430px widths are required, with no page overflow, overlap, clipped labels, or too-small controls.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: Use BNA's first-party Operations and portal shells plus One Time-specific review CSS. Do not introduce GHL, LeadConnector, or external CRM runtime behavior.

requirements.statement: Create and run a repeatable One Time toolbar/filter density audit before broad top-section layout implementation.
requirements.expected_result: A Playwright harness captures topbar/filter measurements and screenshots across Operations, provider, parent, student, and member routes at 1440, 1024, 768, 430, and 390 widths.
acceptance_criteria: Audit checks whole-page horizontal overflow, top cluster height, stacked row count, top control height spread, clipped toolbar control text, mobile tap target size, top control overlap, and first-content vertical position.
Audit writes report.json, report.md, and route/viewport screenshots under ops/ui-audits.
Operations checks authenticate when credentials are available and are explicitly skipped with a reason when not available.
Findings include route, viewport, screenshot, defect code, severity, evidence, and expected fix.

Scoped CSS/layout fixes reduce automated findings from 27 to 6 and remove provider mobile overflow, provider mobile vertical-letter topbar, Operations mobile rail overheight/tap-target findings, member topbar tap-target findings, and One Time email workspace clipping.
No external provider write, private data mutation, payment, access, credential, DNS, send, or production-data mutation is performed.

criteria: Raw intake and parent register already exist.
Existing CSS and smoke scripts were inspected.
The packet role is VISUAL_AUDITOR, so implementation remains forbidden until findings are triaged into a smaller packet.
No external or private-data mutation is required to audit layout.
